steps: Apply online on gun.io with your portfolio and experience.
Have a 1-1 conversation with a Gun.io team member and complete technical vetting (code exercises, references).
Get approved into the vetted developer network.
Receive curated opportunity matches from Gun.io's team (each client job is vetted by a senior developer).
Interview with matched clients and start freelance or full-time engagements.
catches: Vetted network: you must pass technical vetting — many applicants are rejected and earn nothing.
Matching-based, not browse-and-bid: you wait for Gun.io to pitch you to clients rather than picking from open listings.
Freelance engagements are typically structured ongoing commitments, not one-off micro-tasks.
Rates are negotiated per engagement; nothing is guaranteed until a client hires you.
Primarily a developers-only network — non-engineers cannot join as talent.
biggest_catch: You cannot browse and bid on open gigs: Gun.io matches you to clients on its own schedule, so there is no guaranteed volume of opportunities.
eligibility: Experienced software engineers able to pass technical vetting and reference checks.
timing: Vetting then matching on client demand; engagement timing negotiated per client.

c1.evidence: Gun.io's own site states the mechanism: 'each new job seeker who joins the platform has a 1-1 conversation with a member of the team so we can personally pitch them to clients they'd love' and 'Each job posted to the Gun.io platform is vetted by a senior developer.'

c2.evidence: Gun.io publishes no fixed developer pay range — rates negotiated per engagement; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: apply, 1-1 + vetting, approval, curated matching, client interviews.

c4.evidence: Applying and vetting are free for developers; no upfront fee documented.
